headline: US Retail Sales Rise Moderately in October as Import Prices Outpace Estimates
summary: US retail sales posted moderate expansion in October while US import prices increased beyond consensus forecasts. Consumer spending remained resilient despite ongoing inflation pressures.
why: US retail sales data provides a key snapshot of consumer spending, which drives two-thirds of the US economy.

impacts.name: US Dollar Index
impacts.why: Resilient consumer data and higher import inflation support dollar yields on interest rate expectations.
impacts.baseline_rule: first recorded price at or after created_at (15-minute price recorder); end = first price at least 24 h later, within 48 h

why_moved: Solid retail sales and elevated import price metrics boosted the US dollar against foreign currencies.
